 Most recent Most popular A rainy Istanbul published at 17:25 GMT 17:25 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter in Istanbul 
 It has not stopped raining in Istanbul all day but that hasn't stopped the travelling Liverpool fans from enjoying themselves in this great city.
 Just under 2,000 of them have made the journey to Istanbul, which of course has many happy memories for Liverpool. 
 But in recent times, the Turkish capital hasn't been a happy hunting ground for the Reds. 
 They lost twice to Galatasaray last season and haven’t won any of their six away games against Turkish teams in the history of the European Cup/Champions League.

 How realistic that scenario actually is is another matter.

 'I think Barcola can play up front very well' published at 17:20 GMT 17:20 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to TNT Sports: "I think we've been [rotating] basically all the season. You play every three, four days you have to refresh the legs. The defensive positions we don't have as many options.
 "We have injuries but offensively I think we can rotate a little bit and today we can see other players."
 On Bradley Barcola playing as a striker: "I think Bradley, even Victor [Munoz] are players that are wingers but have played sometimes up front. I think we should be mobile.
 "I think we should attack the spaces that are there. They are there to have good combinations outside. We don't expect them to stay there as the nine. I think Bradley can do this job very well."

 A Real-ly good record published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 AEK Athens v Real Madrid (17:45 GMT); Dortmund v Real Betis (20:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images There are two Spanish sides in action this evening and both will be hoping to keep their 100% Champions League record intact. 
 Real Madrid thrashed RB Leipzig 4-1 last time out for their third straight win in Europe this season and Jose Mourinho's side will be looking to extend their winning streak in all competitions to seven games when they travel to AEK Athens tonight.
 Real Betis, meanwhile, have also won all three of their Champions League fixtures with victories over Lille, Porto and Feyenoord.

 It will be a 'very special' night in Istanbul published at 17:13 GMT 17:13 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola expects it to be a "very special" night in Istanbul but, understands that "it won't be easy" for the away side because it never is for English teams that play there.
 "They have very good players in midfield and they have a very good technical level," Iraola said, when discussing what he expects from Turkish giants Fenerbahce.
 "If we allow them a lot of time on the ball and don't press them properly then we will suffer."
 He also wants his side to "continue" their unbeaten run in the Champions League.
 He added: "We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League - three games and nine points. It is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight."

 Opportunity knocks for Nyoni published at 17:09 GMT 17:09 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter in Istanbul 
 Image source, Getty Images Andoni Iraola has called on Trey Nyoni to continue in the same manner after the 19-year-old made his first Premier League start for Liverpool on Sunday.
 With Ryan Gravenberch out of Liverpool's trip to Fenerbahce with a heel injury and a doubt for this Sunday's game against Crystal Palace, Nyoni is set to get more of an opportunity to cement his place as a regular in Liverpool's midfield.
 "I think he has to continue in the same place he has been since pre-season. He's playing most of the games," said Iraola.
 "We trust him, he's doing very well. We have to encourage him to continue improving, learning and getting the experience. He's in very good place."
 Nyoni has already played 513 minutes this season, more than double the 237 minutes he managed last campaign under Arne Slot, stepping up after Liverpool sold Curtis Jones to Inter Milan.
 Asked if Liverpool were ready to rely on Nyoni week in, week out, Iraola stressed that the teenager is getting used to the rhythm of playing two games a week.
 He added: "I think the young players are already playing. Sometimes it's not just playing 90 minutes and 90 minutes.
 "Maybe one day you have to help us play 20 minutes, or another day you have to start and play 65, and then maybe you don't play, maybe you play the full game.
 "He's adding also endurance, because sometimes when you are young, you feel 'OK, I'm not going to get tired'.
 "But you need to add this to your body and give a big effort every three to four days."

 Time for Europe to see how big Fenerbahce is - Kuyt published at 17:02 GMT 17:02 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter in Istanbul 
 Image source, Getty Images Dirk Kuyt insists that it will be a "special occasion" but he will have to park his emotions for Liverpool's Champions League game against Fenerbahce in Istanbul.
 Kuyt - who played for Liverpool between 2006 and 2012 and scored the winning penalty for the Reds in the 2007 Champions League semi-final - is now the interim Fenerbahce boss after Ismail Kartal resigned last week.
 The former Dutch international played for Fenerbahce between 2012 and 2015 and won the Turkish Super Lig. He was Kartal's assistant before stepping up to the role.
 Asked about his feelings pre-match, Kuyt said: "It's a really special achievement for Fenerbahce to be in the Champions League after 18 years and we're really excited. When you reach that stage, you know you'll be playing against very impressive teams.
 "As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me and from that moment, you know it will be a special occasion.
 "Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important - to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance."

 Reds aiming to break duck in Turkey published at 16:59 GMT 16:59 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Liverpool are hoping to continue their perfect start to this year's Champions League but they will need to do something have never done before to maintain that 100% record tonight.
 That's because the Reds haven’t won any of their six away games against Turkish teams in the European Cup/UEFA Champions League, losing five of them (D1), and the last four in a row.
 They have never lost five consecutive away games against sides from one nation in the European Cup/Champions League.
 Of course, Liverpool have enjoyed one very famous victory in Istanbul so it's not all bad memories for them in Turkey...

 Post published at 16:56 GMT 16:56 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Liverpool and Fenerbahce meet for the first time with Andoni Iraola's side having won three from three in the Champions League so far this season.
 A 100% record doesn't quite tell the whole tale after going 2-0 down in their most recent outing at home to Villarreal before prevailing 4-3.
 On Wednesday, they come up against an opposing head coach who reached the final of this competition with the Reds in 2007.
 Dirk Kuyt may be taking charge of his final match as interim boss of the Turkish club, with reports indicating that Sergio Conceicao is set to take over on an 18-month deal.

 Who should Liverpool be worried about? published at 16:54 GMT 16:54 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images The Kosovo striker Vedat Muriqi has scored seven goals despite starting only five league games, but he is yet to break his duck in this competition.
 In the first three matchdays this term, the only player with a higher xG than Muriqi (1.44) who failed to score was Jude Bellingham (1.61).
 Muriqi signed a three-year contract with Fenerbahce in the summer after scoring 23 La Liga goals for Mallorca last season, the best return of his club career.
 He starts on the bench tonight, though, with Romelu Lukaku and Mason Greenwood preferred up top.

 From Derby to Champions League - Brown's journey to face Reds published at 16:51 GMT 16:51 GMT 
 Fenerbahce v Liverpool (17:45 GMT) 
 Aadam Patel 
Football Reporter in Istanbul 
 Image source, Getty Images For Archie Brown, playing for Fenerbahce against Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday will mark another step in the justification of his own "unorthodox" journey that began as a young boy in the Midlands.
 Brown, 24, was born in Birmingham and started his youth career at West Brom before joining Derby, where he helped them to their only youth top-flight title.
 He scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over an Arsenal U18s side that included Bukayo Saka in the final between the North and South division winners.
 Yet come 2021, the Englishman was frustrated by a lack of first-team opportunities and left to join Lausanne Sport in Switzerland at the age of 19.
 "I've had quite an unorthodox journey to get here. I won't say that was always the plan," Brown tells BBC Sport.
 "It was a mixture of two things. I'd seen so many talented players stay on the fringes of the first-team, playing with the U21s and then by 22, 23, they have no real first-team experience.
 "And they have to go down into the lower leagues or non-league to try and build their career up from there. I didn't want to fall victim to that.
 "Secondly, I felt it was important to get out of my environment, to learn a new language, experience a new culture, to help me grow up and mature as a person," Brown adds.
 The left-back - who also plays in central defence and midfield - joined Belgian side Gent in 2023, before moving to Fenerbahce in a £7m deal in 2025.
 The Turkish Super Lig side may be struggling for form - they are sixth and nine points adrift of leaders Galatasaray after 10 games - but Brown is adamant that Andoni Iraola's Liverpool will face an almighty challenge at the 48,000-capacity Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.
